title: Home Comfort Financing Late Fee Amount and Ceiling
content:
**Billing operations note — the amount of a Home Comfort Financing late fee.**

> The late fee posted for a statement period is the scheduled late fee reduced once by the late-fee relief percentage, never more than the plan's late-fee ceiling percentage of the account's monthly payment, and rounded to the cent half up only at the end. The scheduled late fee is the plan's late fee and the late-fee relief percentage is zero.

## The quantities

| Quantity | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Scheduled late fee | the plan's late fee |
| Late-fee relief percentage | zero |
| Fee after relief | the scheduled late fee multiplied by the difference between 100 and the late-fee relief percentage, and divided by 100 |
| Ceiling | the plan's late-fee ceiling percentage multiplied by the account's monthly payment (as set at funding), divided by 100 |
| Late fee posted | the lower of the fee after relief and the ceiling, rounded to the cent half up |

The ceiling is measured against the monthly payment recorded on the account. Rounding happens once, on the final figure; no intermediate figure is rounded.

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

*Ceiling not reached.* Scheduled late fee $39.00, relief percentage zero, ceiling percentage 100, monthly payment $190.61. Fee after relief: $39.00. Ceiling: $190.61. The lower is $39.00, so $39.00 is posted.

*Ceiling reached.* Same plan figures, monthly payment $35.00. Fee after relief: $39.00. Ceiling: 100 percent of $35.00, which is $35.00. The lower is $35.00, so $35.00 is posted.

*Ceiling equal to the fee.* Monthly payment $39.00: the fee after relief and the ceiling are both $39.00, and $39.00 is posted.

## Points of judgement

- The ceiling applies to the fee after relief, before rounding.
- A statement period carries at most one late fee; this note fixes the amount of that one fee.
